title: NGC 3582 - The Heart of a Stellar Nursery
caption: NGC 3582 in the star-forming region RCW 57, imaged by the Gemini South telescope

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Glowing gas and dark clouds of dust mingle among newly formed stars in this Gemini South view of NGC 3582, which lies at the center of the star-forming region RCW 57 in the far-southern constellation Carina. Ultraviolet radiation from the young stars energizes the gas and makes it glow.

The intricate wisps in the cloud are sculpted by that radiation and by the explosions of nearby, very massive stars, which live exceptionally short lives compared with stars like the Sun. A 2006 study by M. Maercker found the region unusually rich in massive star formation, with more than 33 star-forming regions in the wider area in the final stages of formation.

The region can only be seen from the southern hemisphere, where it is a popular sight for small telescopes and binoculars. The picture is a mosaic of two pointings with the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph, covering 9.0 by 5.0 arcminutes. It was taken through three narrowband filters, with oxygen shown in blue, sulfur in green and hydrogen-alpha in red.

understand.summary: Taken in visible light with the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph on Gemini South through narrowband filters, with [O III] shown as blue, [S II] as green and hydrogen-alpha as red.
understand.eye: Narrow filters isolate the glow of individual gases, and the long exposures gather far more light than the eye, so the colors are much stronger than a telescope view.
